1920s.1920: Founded as Toyo Cork Kogyo - cork manufacturing
1920s.1927: Renamed Toyo Kogyo, diversified into machining tools

1930s.1931: First motorized vehicle - Mazda-Go three-wheeled truck
1930s.1936: Adopted 'Mazda' name for vehicles (from Ahura Mazda)

1940s.1945: Hiroshima factory survived atomic bomb - aided city recovery

1950s.1958: First passenger car prototype - the R360 Coupe development begins
1950s.1959: Mazda and NSU (Germany) begin Wankel rotary engine collaboration

1960s.1960: R360 Coupe - first Mazda passenger car
1960s.1961: Technical agreement with NSU for Wankel rotary development
1960s.1967: Cosmo Sport 110S - world's first production twin-rotor Wankel car
1960s.1968: Familia Rotary R100 - first volume rotary production car

1970s.1971: Savanna RX-3 launched - racing legend begins
1970s.1974: Partnership with Ford Motor Company begins
1970s.1978: RX-7 (SA22C/FB) launched - iconic rotary sports car

1980s.1984: Company officially renamed Mazda Motor Corporation
1980s.1985: 626 becomes first Japanese car manufactured in USA (Flat Rock, MI)
1980s.1989: MX-5 Miata (NA) launched - revives roadster segment
Mazda 787B development begins for Le Mans

1990s.1991: 787B wins Le Mans 24 Hours - only rotary victory

2000s.2003: RX-8 with Renesis engine - Engine of the Year
2000s.2008: Ford reduces stake amid financial crisis

2010s.2010: Ford divests to 3% stake - Mazda independent again
2010s.2012: RX-8 production ends - last production rotary
2010s.2019: Skyactiv-X SPCCI engine debuts - first production compression ignition gasoline

2020s.2021: Rotary returns as range extender in MX-30
2020s.2023: Inline-6 Skyactiv 3.3L and CX-60/90 platform launch
